name: Shadow-Mode Vial Inspection Benchmark
description: This project is a reproducible, public-data benchmark evaluating whether frontier vision-language models (VLMs) and decision models can be trusted in the decision step of pharmaceutical parenteral vial inspection. It is explicitly not a GMP line qualification; it is an open evaluation template built on the public ResiDual dataset (Rosati, Marchesini, Lumetti, et al., “Identifying Impurities in Liquids of Pharmaceutical Vials,” ICPR 2024, DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-78447-7_18; 730 spin-stop sequences, 13,880 frames, five classes). Dataset images are not redistributed here — they are linked to UNIMORE AImageLab and the authors are cited; this project releases only code, model predictions, metrics, and per-call audit trails. The purpose is to measure frontier AI against a trained CNN baseline and ground truth using the regulated metric vocabulary that quality and regulatory reviewers actually rely on — recall/sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy, AUROC, silent-miss rate, calibration (Expected Calibration Error), and false-reject recovery — rather than the single accuracy number typically reported. Two linked studies are included: Study 1 scores a trained ResNet-18 baseline against a zero-shot panel of frontier VLMs and a decision-model arm on a held-out, sequence-level split (no frame leakage; seed 42; manifest frozen).
